claims.claim_text: The indexed Felix Gilbert is the historian whose archived curriculum vitae records OSS Research and Analysis service from July 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name, NARA index entry, archived first-person career chronology, and NARA Research and Analysis staff list align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The curriculum vitae dates Institute membership through 1943 and OSS service from July 1943.
claims.match_notes: The archived curriculum vitae provides a person-specific chronology rather than a namesake inference.

claims.claim_text: Gilbert's immediate documented pre-OSS institutional affiliation was membership at the Institute for Advanced Study.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: His archived curriculum vitae places Institute membership in 1939-1943 directly before OSS service beginning in July 1943.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded; the source does not supply a day-level end date for the Institute membership.
claims.match_notes: Membership is presented as an institutional affiliation, not presumed employment.

claims.claim_text: Gilbert taught in the History Department at Scripps College in 1936-1937.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The archived curriculum vitae directly names the institution, department, function, and years.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; later Institute membership intervened before OSS.
claims.match_notes: The record does not establish Scripps as the last civilian employer before OSS.

claims.claim_text: Gilbert taught in a Brooklyn College summer school during the 1936-1937 period.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The archived curriculum vitae names Brooklyn College among Gilbert's summer-school teaching posts.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; exact summer and sequence are not stated.
claims.match_notes: This is not labeled as the final pre-OSS employer.

claims.claim_text: Gilbert taught in a Colorado College summer school during the 1936-1937 period.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The archived curriculum vitae names Colorado College among Gilbert's summer-school teaching posts.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; exact summer and sequence are not stated.
claims.match_notes: This is not labeled as the final pre-OSS employer.

claims.evidence_paraphrase: The archived curriculum vitae names the University of Denver among Gilbert's summer-school teaching posts.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; exact summer and sequence are not stated.
claims.match_notes: This is not labeled as the final pre-OSS employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed P-7 Franz L. Neumann is the political and legal scholar who joined OSS Research and Analysis in February 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, civilian grade, person-specific scholarly chronology, and NARA Research and Analysis staff list align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The scholarly chapter dates full-time U.S. government and OSS work from February 22, 1943.
claims.match_notes: The person-specific employment chronology and official NARA staff list distinguish Franz L. Neumann from Sigmund Neumann in the same index box.

claims.claim_text: Neumann's probable immediate pre-OSS government affiliation was the U.S. Board of Economic Warfare.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: He divided time with the Board during summer and fall 1942 before entering full-time government and OSS service in February 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Franz L. Neumann.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate sequence; the source does not document an exact Board-to-OSS transfer.
claims.match_notes: Published with visible qualification and excluded from default high-confidence immediate-affiliation analytics.

claims.claim_text: The Institute for Social Research was Neumann's last documented civilian employer before full-time federal and OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The scholarly chapter dates termination from the Institute to the end of 1942 and federal service to February 22, 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Franz L. Neumann.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded, with an intervening part-time Board of Economic Warfare assignment modeled separately.
claims.match_notes: The Institute is not collapsed into Columbia University, and the Board assignment is not mislabeled as civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Haje Holborn is historian Hajo Holborn, the Yale professor who joined the OSS Research and Analysis Branch.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive surname, close given-name spelling variant, Yale chronology, GHI OSS pathway, and NARA staff list align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Yale dates the professorship from 1934; the GHI project identifies Holborn as coming from Yale to the OSS section.
claims.match_notes: The index spelling Haje remains preserved, while Hajo is added as a documented variant rather than silently substituted.

claims.claim_text: Holborn's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was his Yale University history professorship.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Yale documents the professorship from 1934, and the GHI project describes Holborn as coming from Yale to the OSS section.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit institutional-to-OSS pathway; the Yale appointment continued during and after wartime service.
claims.match_notes: The continuing academic appointment is treated as an overlapping affiliation, not forced into an artificial end date.

claims.claim_text: Yale University was Holborn's documented civilian employer when he entered OSS work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional finding aid documents his continuous Yale professorship, and the GHI account links that Yale position to his OSS recruitment.
claims.temporal_assessment: The employment overlapped wartime OSS service rather than ending before it.
claims.match_notes: No later civilian employer is inserted between Yale and OSS.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Edward M. Earle is Institute for Advanced Study professor Edward Mead Earle, who helped organize OSS Research and Analysis.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, Institute scholar record, and contemporary Institute report of his 1941-1942 OSS role align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The contemporary bulletin dates his OSS organizing work to 1941 and 1942 during his Institute faculty appointment.
claims.match_notes: The institutional bulletin gives the specific OSS function, avoiding a fame-based namesake assignment.

claims.claim_text: Earle's immediate documented civilian affiliation when he began OSS work was the Institute for Advanced Study.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Institute dates his faculty appointment from 1934 and records that he assisted OSS Research and Analysis organization in 1941-1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Edward Mead Earle.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded continuing affiliation; it overlapped his OSS assistance.
claims.match_notes: The Institute appointment is not given a false wartime termination date.

claims.claim_text: The Institute for Advanced Study was Earle's documented civilian employer when he began assisting OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Institute scholar record and contemporary bulletin establish continuous faculty employment and the wartime OSS role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Edward Mead Earle.
claims.temporal_assessment: The civilian appointment continued during wartime government consulting.
claims.match_notes: The evidence supports an overlapping employer relationship, not a completed prewar job followed by an undocumented gap.

claims.claim_text: The indexed P-5 Sigmund Neumann is the Wesleyan political scientist documented in scholarly literature as an OSS worker.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name, civilian grade, Wesleyan faculty chronology, and scholarly OSS identification align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Wesleyan dates continuous faculty service from 1934; the scholarly review places his OSS work during that career.
claims.match_notes: The Wesleyan chronology and full-name scholarly OSS identification distinguish him from Franz L. Neumann in the same index box.

claims.claim_text: Sigmund Neumann's immediate documented civilian affiliation when he undertook OSS work was Wesleyan University.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Wesleyan documents his uninterrupted faculty sequence from 1934, and a scholarly review identifies his wartime OSS work.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded continuing affiliation; an exact OSS appointment day remains to be confirmed.
claims.match_notes: The continuing Wesleyan appointment is not assigned an artificial wartime end date.

claims.claim_text: Wesleyan University was Sigmund Neumann's documented civilian employer during his OSS work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official department history establishes the faculty employment, while the scholarly review establishes the overlapping OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The civilian appointment overlapped OSS work.
claims.match_notes: The evidence supports Wesleyan as an ongoing civilian employer, not merely an educational affiliation.
